bottom_line: In EUROPA, perindopril 8 mg once daily vs placebo reduced the primary composite of cardiovascular mortality, MI, or cardiac arrest with a 20% relative risk reduction (95% CI 9 to 29).
implications: These results support that, in this population, perindopril reduced the composite primary endpoint from 9.9% to 8.0% over 4.2 years (relative risk reduction 20% [95% CI 9 to 29]) and produced a reported 1.9% absolute risk reduction; the document also reports an estimate that about 50 patients would need treatment for 4 years to prevent one major cardiovascular event. The evidence does not establish a statistically significant reduction in cardiovascular mortality alone (14% [–3 to 28], p=0.107) or total mortality alone (11% [–2 to 23], p=0.1) as reported here.

major_points.text: Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicentre trial in stable coronary heart disease without apparent heart failure.
major_points.quote: We did a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicentre study.

major_points.text: After a 4-week run-in in which all patients received perindopril, 12 218 were randomised to perindopril 8 mg daily or placebo.
major_points.quote: After a run-in period of 4 weeks, in which all patients received perindopril, 12 218 patients were randomly assigned perindopril 8 mg once daily (n=6110), or matching placebo (n=6108).

major_points.text: Primary endpoint was a composite of cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, and cardiac arrest with successful resuscitation.
major_points.quote: The primary endpoint was a composite of cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, and cardiac arrest with successful resuscitation.

major_points.text: Cough and hypotension were more common reasons for permanent treatment withdrawal with perindopril than placebo.

absolute_effects.text: Primary endpoint event rates: 488 (8.0%) with perindopril vs 603 (9.9%) with placebo.
Absolute risk reduction for the primary endpoint: 1.9%.
absolute_effects.quote:
This finding yields a
      20% relative risk reduction (95% CI 9–29, table 3), and
      a 1·9% absolute risk reduction.

absolute_effects.text: Estimated number needed to treat: about 50 patients treated for 4 years to prevent one major cardiovascular event.
absolute_effects.quote:
We estimate that 50 patients need to
      be treated with perindopril for a period of 4 years, to
      prevent one major cardiovascular event.

absolute_effects.text: Heart failure requiring hospital admission: 63 (1.0%) with perindopril vs 103 (1.7%) with placebo.

subgroups.text: A descriptive analysis of the primary endpoint was done in clinically defined subgroups of patients.
subgroups.quote:
A descriptive analysis of the primary endpoint was also
     done in clinically defined subgroups of patients.

subgroups.text: Beneficial effect on the primary endpoint was consistent across all predefined subgroups.
subgroups.quote:
The beneficial effect of perindopril on the primary
      endpoint was consistent across all predefined subgroups

harms.text: Permanent treatment withdrawal occurred in 22.8% with perindopril vs 20.7% with placebo.
Cough as a reason for permanent treatment withdrawal: 2.7% perindopril vs 0.5% placebo.
Hypotension as a reason for permanent treatment withdrawal: 1.0% perindopril vs 0.3% placebo.
Kidney failure as a reason for permanent treatment withdrawal: 0.3% in both groups.
